proposals.evidence: Full ma explicitly explains the replacement of old aham by the oblique/instrumental pronoun (Prakrit maē, Apabhramsha maï̃), listing Assamese maï, Bengali mui, Oriya mu/mũ and Punjabi/Lahnda maĩ/mɛ̃. These whole first-person singular responses match those regional nominative continuations, preserving length, nasalization and source vowel notation. They are not assigned to aham merely from their nominative function; accusative molā and additional case endings are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Section 2 naviya explicitly gives Prakrit ṇavia and Hindi/Bihari nayā, with feminine naī. These Tharu survey nayā/nayā̃ forms preserve the full y-bearing masculine adjective and fit that branch. The comparative-family relation does not settle whether Hindi transmission helped spread this form locally; bare nai forms ambiguous with nava feminine are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Turner separates section 4 *chaggala, with Bihari chāgar/chāgrī and Awadhi chagarī “goat”, from the contracted chēl branch. These selected Danuwar, Majhi and Tharu c(h)agar/cegar forms retain medial g and r and match that specific regional branch. Extra -iyā material is excluded; local borrowing remains unresolved by the comparative link.
